referents.why: Dative 'to them' is the crowd Pilate wants to satisfy and to whom Barabbas is released. Crowd is in this verse's candidates, and the plural pronoun agrees with the collective.
Subject of 'delivered' and 'had ... flogged' is Pilate, the subject of 'released' in the same verse. The builder's null is filled.
The passive subjunctive 'might be crucified' has as its subject the one crucified, Jesus (w16). It is not Pilate, so the builder's cl3s is wrong.

links.why: The participle 'wishing' takes the infinitive 'to satisfy' as its complement, a verb of wanting.
links.category: complement of a verb of wanting

links.why: The wishing participle is nested in the release clause as an adjunct.
The flogging participle is a prior act of Pilate that stands as its own event ('had Jesus flogged'), so it is nested, not describing.
Greek hina with the subjunctive: the handing over is for the crucifixion. This is what the act is for.
The infinitive cl2 is nested inside cl1 inside cl0. A nested clause does not link forward to its own host as 'and then'.
links.category: nested clause linked to its host

links.why: The connective is de (kai), adversative, not a fused waw. 'And then' is not supported by the form; the relation the text carries is contrast, added below.
links.category: connective is not a fused waw

links.why: Mid-verse adversative de: 'But he had Jesus flogged' sets Pilate's release of Barabbas against his handing over of Jesus. The host is cl0.

groups.why: Proposed reading for review. Pilate's acts in a row: released Barabbas (cl0), had Jesus flogged and handed him over (cl3). Each states its subject only in the verb, and all resolve to Pilate.
groups.category: one agent's acts in a row (reading)

none_fit.what: The implied object of the participle, Jesus, is not in the slot list.
